PullRequest.Title: Let the HydraFusion setting select v2
PullRequest.Body:

Stacked on #340212 (Copilot SDK `1.0.17-preview.8`, which ships the HydraFusion v2 runtime changes). Please review that first; this PR's own change is the top commit.

Lets the existing HydraFusion setting select **HydraFusion v2**, so v2 can be A/B tested without adding a new setting.

### Setting
`chat.copilot.hydraFusion.enabled` now accepts:
- `true`: HydraFusion (v1), the existing default and behavior
- `false`: off
- `"v2"`: HydraFusion v2

The setting is already experiment-controlled (`experiment: { mode: 'startup' }`), so the experiment only needs to assign `"v2"` to the existing `config.chat.copilot.hydraFusion.enabled` treatment in the treatment arm, with `true` in control. Unknown values are treated as off.

### Agent host
- The workbench maps the value to two agent-host root config booleans, `hydraFusion` (unchanged) and the new `hydraFusionV2`, both still gated by the preview-features policy. The agent host's existing `hydraFusion === true` checks don't change.
- When `hydraFusionV2` is on, the session launcher adds the runtime's `HYDRAFUSION_PLAN_V2` session feature flag next to `HYDRAFUSION`/`HYDRAFUSION_ROLLOUT`.
- `hydraFusionV2` is part of `CopilotAgentStartupConfig`. Session feature flags aren't reapplied when a resident SDK session resumes, so switching versions restarts the runtime, just like toggling HydraFusion.
- `HYDRAFUSION_PLAN_V2` is stripped from the inherited environment like the other HydraFusion flags, so only the setting controls it.

### Experiment trigger
`experimentTrigger` for `config.chat.copilot.hydraFusion.enabled` is logged when a live `session.fusion_route_started` is accepted for the current turn, i.e. where the runtime routes as v1 or v2. It fires in every arm, and is held until the workbench forwards the assignment context (same pattern as other agent-host triggers).

### Validation
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostCopilotCliSettingsContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentStartupConfig.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts`: 986 passing, 0 failing (covers the value → root config mapping, the launcher flags, the restart config, and the trigger in both arms and while waiting for assignment context)
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --grep 'strips inherited HydraFusion flags|publishes HydraFusion'`: 2 passing. Locally, 13 other tests in this file fail identically without this change because they read the real `~/.copilot` directory.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no new errors (only pre-existing missing `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` in my local `node_modules`)

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting HydraFusion off, v1, or v2 and forwarding the setting into a running local agent host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The setting or preview-policy event recomputes the HydraFusion and HydraFusionV2 root keys, dispatches only changed values to the local agent host, applies each root action, persists root config, and requests a Copilot runtime restart when the startup snapshot changes. If a turn is active, restart is explicitly deferred until chats are idle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch RootConfigChanged actions from the workbench to the local agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to two actions per HydraFusion setting/policy transition after equality filtering; true-to-v2 is one action, while off-to-v2 can be two.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boolean setting controlled one HydraFusion root key and could dispatch at most one action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to apply the selected runtime version before subsequent launches; fixed cardinality and not tied to session or workspace size.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and persist the complete agent-host root configuration after each accepted RootConfigChanged action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two serialized writes for an off-to-v2 transition; otherwise generally one, with writes sequenced by _rootConfigWrite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A HydraFusion boolean transition caused at most one persistence request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence is scheduled from config handling but is not awaited by the workbench setting path; the added maximum is one write on the rare two-key transition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop the existing Copilot SDK client/runtime so the next session starts with the selected feature flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one effective stop for one logical version transition; pending requests coalesce while busy, and immediate stop clears pending reasons before awaiting client.stop().
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: On/off HydraFusion changes already restarted the runtime; the diff extends that existing boundary to v1/v2 changes without increasing restart count per transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred off active turns, but the next chat may wait for or initiate a fresh runtime start. This is required because resident sessions do not reapply session feature flags.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single setting/policy transition affects two fixed root keys. false-to-v2 or v2-to-false can change both keys; true-to-v2 changes only the v2 key after structural equality filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two per-key forwarder pushes can begin independently, but each has a structural equality guard. On the host, busy-chat restart requests accumulate in a Set and are applied once when idle; an immediate stop clears pending reasons synchronously and makes the client unavailable before awaiting subprocess shutdown.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The live root-state values act as a warm equality cache, suppressing unchanged dispatches. On cold hydration or a newly introduced key, the missing value is forwarded once and then persisted; there is no repeated negative-cache miss.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the two-key forwarding, equality filtering, persistence, and restart coalescing paths from the forwarder, host action handler, and Copilot client lifecycle code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and IPC duration vary by platform, but multiplicity is fixed at two keys and setting/policy changes are infrequent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the extra config action/write is bounded and rare, and the expensive subprocess lifecycle is deliberately deferred/coalesced rather than duplicated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating or resuming a Copilot session with HydraFusion v2 selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session launch reads the two root booleans, builds the existing featureFlags object, then follows the unchanged SDK create/resume path. A cold client may require the existing runtime subprocess startup; a resident client is reused when its startup configuration matches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or reuse the Copilot runtime process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one runtime client per existing lifecycle; no additional spawn is added for each v2 session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: HydraFusion v1 used the same runtime lifecycle and startup invalidation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold runtime startup remains on the existing session-launch path; the new boolean only selects startup/session metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume the SDK session with the assembled featureFlags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing SDK create/resume operation per session launch; adding HYDRAFUSION_PLAN_V2 does not add another call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create/resume operation already carried HydraFusion feature flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary remains required for session availability; payload growth is one small property.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time pair of config reads and one optional feature-flag property per session launch/resume, independent of plugin, model, workspace, or history cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing session launch sequencing and concurrent BYOK/shell/custom-agent preparation are unchanged. The added flag does not start new parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resident client is reused while the startup snapshot is unchanged. Changing the v2 value invalidates that lifecycle once via CopilotAgentStartupConfig; feature flags are rebuilt per launch as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that host-side work added by the diff is constant-size metadata construction with unchanged boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external v2 runtime's own model-planning cost is outside the supplied diff; this code only selects it and does not establish an added host-side call or allocation mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the diff adds a constant-size flag to an existing launch payload and correctly scopes restart invalidation to version changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Accepting live HydraFusion routing events and logging the experiment trigger
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An accepted current-turn session.fusion_route_started event checks assignment-context availability and, once available, calls the experiment-trigger helper before continuing through the existing fusion progress reducer. If context is absent, one boolean is retained and a later root-config event retries in a microtask.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue one experimentTrigger telemetry event through ITelemetryService.publicLog2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one emitted event per telemetry service for config.chat.copilot.hydraFusion.enabled, regardless of route count or session count in that process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No HydraFusion-version experiment trigger was emitted from this event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The local telemetry enqueue occurs on the first accepted route; subsequent routes are deduplicated and no direct awaited network operation is added to turn progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The lightweight check executes once per accepted routing event, but telemetry emission is deduplicated to one event per telemetry service/treatment for the process lifetime. Deferred state is one boolean, not a per-event collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event handling remains synchronous except for a single queued microtask on a root-config change while the trigger is pending. Multiple routes do not launch concurrent network requests because logExperimentTrigger uses a per-service Set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold behavior emits one trigger after assignment context exists. Warm behavior performs a Set membership check and emits nothing. Pending assignment context is represented by a bounded boolean and is cleared after successful reporting.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in fixed retained state and one-time emission from the helper implementation and accepted-event call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact telemetry backend batching is not visible in the reviewed path, but the helper's process-wide one-event cap and non-awaited call are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the only scaling work is a small map/schema lookup per route, while expensive telemetry emission is bounded to one and no unbounded event retention is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 13 changed files and traced settings propagation, root-config persistence, Copilot runtime restart/launch, session feature-flag assembly, environment sanitization, and fusion-route telemetry. Added boundary work is fixed-cardinality, equality-filtered, deduplicated, or lifecycle-coalesced; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
